summary: Round 3 full review of all 16 units. Every numeric key, worked example and table was recomputed with scripts (Routh arrays and root counts including 0.288+-1.416j, 0.223+-2.01j and the (s+6)(s^2+k) factorisations; breakaway points -0.903, -4.975 (K=1.25), -0.845, -0.465; centroids; margins and the zeta/PM/overshoot table; Bode, resonance and decibel values; Ziegler-Nichols and PI tuning; physical models; and the Euler/RK4 and saturated-servo simulations, which reproduce 16.6/35.1/2.6 percent overshoot, 5.74/13.78/3.16 s settling and the 1.162-1.422 peak table). Both round-2 fixes verify: the Bode callout now gives 7.96, 13.98 and 20.00 dB for zeta=0.2, 0.1 and 0.05, and the DC-motor warning is correct (JR/(bR+K^2)=1e-4/0.00252=0.0397 s, J/b=5 s, ratio about 126, DC gain 19.8 rad/s per V, 12 V gives 238 rad/s about 2274 rpm, and the integrator wording is now properly qualified). The string scan found no tabs or control characters, no non-ASCII text, no format placeholders, no e+06 numbers, no bare x or 	imes10 outside math, no placeholder steps and no stale option-letter references. Only one cosmetic minor remains. This is an AI review only: the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

issues.problem: In the margins worked example the phase step reads '-90-37.2-16.9=-144.1 degrees, so PM = 35.8 degrees' but the accompanying latex says 'PM=180-144.2=35.8'. The two phase values differ (144.1 vs 144.2) and 180-144.1 would give 35.9; the exact phase is -144.17 degrees and PM = 35.83 degrees.
issues.suggestedFix: Use one rounded value in both places, for example '-144.2 degrees' (37.3+16.9 rounded consistently) in the text and the latex, giving PM = 35.8 degrees.
